title: Evaluate Valid Expressions
summary: Given a string expression representing a nested mathematical expression, evaluate it.
statement: Given a string expression representing a nested mathematical expression, evaluate it. The expression is either an integer or follows the format op(a,b) where op is one of 'add', 'sub', 'mul', or 'div'. The operations are defined as: add(a,b) = a + b, sub(a,b) = a - b, mul(a,b) = a * b, and div(a,b) = a / b. Return the integer result of the fully evaluated expression.
constraints: expression is a valid integer literal or nested add, sub, mul, or div call up to 100,000 characters.
Each operation has exactly two comma-separated operands.
All divisions are exact and all intermediate values fit a signed long integer.
hints: The grammar is fully parenthesized, so a closing parenthesis completes exactly one pending binary operation.
Scan tokens onto a stack; on a close, pop the two values, marker, and operator, then push the result.
Parse signed integer literals and operation names directly without recursion.
Stack nesting mirrors grammar nesting, so each reduction evaluates one complete innermost expression before its parent.
editorial: Stack nesting mirrors grammar nesting, so each reduction evaluates one complete innermost expression before its parent.
